summary: Iteration 884 — Apple/Basic IAP production-e2e scenario (David Thomas @ 6606 ARANCIONE AVE, San Antonio, TX 72533) verified end-to-end via 8-test pytest suite (100% 8/8 pass, ~11s). All 4 endpoint checks (fee_accuracy, notification_latency_under_2s, subscription_active, api_integrity) return true. Apple/Basic/TX pricing exactly matches problem-statement target: base 5.99 + platform_fee 1.91 (30%) + TX tax 0.37 (6.25%) = final_total 8.27. payment_transactions row shows provider='iap_apple', tax_rate=0.0625, jurisdiction={country:'US', state:'TX', postal_code:'72533', city:'San Antonio', address_line:'6606 ARANCIONE AVE'}, status='completed', notification_sent=true (flipped within ~1s). User record: name='David Thomas', subscription_plan='basic', subscription_status='active', iap_platform='apple', billing_address_line='6606 ARANCIONE AVE'. In-app notification (type='payment_confirmation') title='Payment Successful — Basic Plan Activated' and message contains $8.27 + 'App Store' + IAP- eTicket id. Plan-transition timeline verified: sequential premium/google → basic/apple on same fresh test email recorded db.iap_subscription_timeline event with event_type='downgrade', from_plan='premium', to_plan='basic', platform='apple' (30-min duplicate-suppression correctly bypassed because (provider,plan,period) tuple changed). Backend log signals confirmed for the Apple/App Store variant: '[Resend] ... subject=Subscription Confirmed — Receipt Enclosed' (no mojibake), 'Branded receipt email sent' (user PDF path), Resend admin subject '[Admin] Payment Confirmed via App Store — RCT-...', and 'Admin payment receipt email sent' line all present. simulate_failure_case=false correctly produces failure_case=null with zero payment-failed lines near the fresh tx_id. Regression: GET /api/iap/admin/compliance-bundles/{apple_tx_id}/receipt.pdf returns 200 application/pdf with %PDF magic bytes. NO email sent to kadjimonn@gmail.com — all test emails are iap.e2e.iter884.<uuid>@example.com.
critical_code_review_comments: iap.py remains ~2881 lines (well over the 700-line threshold flagged in iter883). No new regressions in this iteration; recommend the same follow-up refactor into routes/iap/ package (checkout, subscriptions, admin_simulation, compliance).

simulate_iap_production_e2e (~line 2005) forwards body.address_line into parsed_success without strip(). While the create/update paths at lines 1974/1982 correctly strip and skip empty strings, the jurisdiction persisted on payment_transactions.jurisdiction.address_line will keep leading/trailing whitespace verbatim if the operator passes it. Cosmetic — strip once at the top and reuse.

The plan-transition scenario relies on the (user, provider, plan, period) suppression tuple to differentiate emails — this is correct behavior and matches the real kadjimonn sequence, but is nowhere documented in code comments near _apply_iap_subscription. Recommend a 2-line docstring above _apply_iap_subscription describing the suppression key so future refactors don't break it.

Motor client shared via `from routes.db import db` is bound to whichever event loop imports it first, causing 'Event loop is closed' failures when two @pytest.mark.asyncio tests both read it (pytest-asyncio strict mode creates a fresh loop per test). Iter884 works around this by using sync pymongo for the second async test. Long-term: expose an async fixture that returns a per-test AsyncIOMotorClient bound to the current loop, or use motor's ioloop kwarg in a fixture. Not blocking, but hits every future testing agent.
test_credentials: Admin: admin@realaicoach.app / NewAdminPass2026! (cookie-based /api/auth/login; X-Requested-With: XMLHttpRequest header required for POST past CSRF middleware). Test emails: iap.e2e.iter884.<uuid>@example.com — 5-8 fresh users seeded per run.
seed_data_creation: Each test run creates 5-8 fresh users prefixed 'iap.e2e.iter884.<uuid>@example.com' (some also carry 'iap.e2e.iter884.tr.' for the transition test), with corresponding payment_transactions, notifications, iap_subscription_timeline events, and iap_compliance_bundles rows. All are TEST_-analog (namespaced by unique prefix) and left in-place for main-agent inspection. Volume per run is <10 users. NO production data modified. kadjimonn@gmail.com was NOT re-emailed.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Reusable pytest file: /app/backend/tests/test_iap_production_e2e_iter884.py (8 tests, ~11s). Same admin cookie-session + X-Requested-With CSRF pattern as iter883. Notable new patterns for future iterations: (a) TX/Apple/Basic pricing regression target 5.99+1.91+0.37=8.27 with tax_rate=0.0625; (b) admin log-subject differs by store — Apple = '[Admin] Payment Confirmed via App Store — RCT-...', Google = '[Admin] Payment Confirmed via Google Play — RCT-...'; (c) the plan-downgrade timeline test uses sync pymongo (not motor) to avoid pytest-asyncio event-loop rebinding across two async tests that both share the module-level motor client at routes.db.db — copy this pattern when a suite needs multiple async db-reading tests. (d) 30-min duplicate suppression is keyed by (user, provider, plan, period), so a fresh scenario in the same test email STILL fires a new notification if provider or plan or period changes — this is what makes the premium/google → basic/apple downgrade path testable in-suite.
rca of the issue: No production bug found in this iteration — this run is a scenario-coverage extension of iter883, not a bug fix. All previously-fixed defects (mojibake receipt subject, missing name/address_line, simulate_failure_case default true) remain fixed under the Apple/Basic/TX variant. The one intra-test issue encountered — 'Event loop is closed' when two @pytest.mark.asyncio tests both read `from routes.db import db` — is a test-infra issue (motor client bound to the first-imported loop, pytest-asyncio strict mode allocates fresh loop per function). Mitigated in this suite by switching the second async test to sync pymongo. Recommendation for main agent: consider adding a session-scoped async db fixture that constructs a fresh AsyncIOMotorClient tied to the current event loop for tests, but this is a QA-side ergonomics fix and not a production defect.
